newsitem.title: CYPRUS: British AIDS woman knew I had virus-Cypriot lover.
newsitem.headline: British AIDS woman knew I had virus-Cypriot lover.

text.p: A Greek Cypriot accused by his former British lover of infecting her with the killer AIDS virus told police she may have had the disease before he slept with her, a Cyprus court heard on Thursday.

In a statement to police read out in court, 40-year-old fisherman Pavlos Georgiou also insisted his former lover knew in advance that he was HIV positive, dismissing her earlier claims that he kept his condition a secret from her.

"If a woman knows that her sex partner is an AIDS carrier and she is not, why did she insist on making love without any precautions? In my opinion only a woman who is also a carrier of AIDS would do such a thing," Georgiou said in a statement to police taken in January this year.
Last week the court, in the coastal town of Larnaca, heard Janette Pink, 45, from Basildon, Essex, say that Georgiou consistently lied to her about his condition during their three-year affair.
His English-Cypriot wife Martha died of an AIDS-related illness in August 1994. Pink said Georgiou told her she died of leukaemia.
Pink tested HIV positive in October 1994, nine months after her affair with Georgiou, a local fisherman and builder, started. Pink returned to Britain last year after her condition deteriorated.
She has now got just a few years to live, while Georgiou, a widower with four children, is HIV positive but has no apparent signs he is suffering from any illness.
Georgiou has denied the accusations. He is charged that through negligence he committed an act that could transmit the infection of a life-threatening disease.
The charge carries a prison sentence of up to two years in jail, a 1,500 Cyprus pound fine, or both.

Occasionally repeating himself, Georgiou said in the four-page statement that Pink knew he had the AIDS virus before he slept with her. Once their relationship turned physical she insisted on not taking any precautions, he said.
"I can't remember specifically when we made love without my taking any precautions but I assure you it was when Janette knew I was an AIDS carrier," he said.

The statement was accepted in court as evidence after a failed bid by defence lawyers to get it thrown out as inadmissible. Defence lawyer Tassos Economou said police had taken the statement from Georgiou without cautioning him on its legal implications, giving him assurances it was just a formality to close the case.
